name: AI Engineering from Scratch
tagline: A free 523-lesson curriculum that teaches AI engineering by building real projects - from zero to running systems in production.
sentence: Work through 523 lessons across 20 phases, each one a real coding exercise in Python, TypeScript, Rust or Julia - from 'what is a neural network' to putting a working AI system online, with no video lectures and no paywall.

board.say: You want to learn AI engineering, but courses are either too theoretical (lectures and slides) or too expensive (bootcamps at $5,000+).
board.eg: A Coursera specialization costs $49/month and takes 6 months. A bootcamp costs $5,000-15,000. Neither gives you real code to run.

board.say: You open the curriculum on GitHub or the website and start with Phase 0, Lesson 1.
board.eg: Go to the website, pick a phase that matches your level, and open the first lesson. Each one is a file you run.

board.say: Your time and a computer. Lessons are self-contained files you read, modify and run.
board.eg: Each lesson is a Python, TypeScript, Rust or Julia file with comments explaining what it does and exercises at the end.

board.say: It walks you through 20 phases of AI engineering, from fundamentals to putting real systems online, with 523 hands-on exercises.
steps: Phase 0: Foundations - Python, math, hardware (GPU setup, container basics)

Phases 1-10: Core AI - neural networks, transformers, fine-tuning (adjusting an AI model with your own data), RAG (retrieval-augmented generation - teaching AI to look up facts before answering), agents
Phases 11-20: Production - putting systems online, monitoring, security, multi-agent systems, AI engineering for teams
board.eg: Phase 3, Lesson 7: build a small transformer model from scratch in Python, train it on text, and watch it learn to predict the next word.

board.say: Practical AI engineering skills, demonstrated by the code you wrote and the systems you built.

outputs.eg: 523 files you wrote and ran, covering the full stack from fundamentals to production

outputs.what: A structured path from zero to production
outputs.eg: 20 phases that build on each other - you don't have to guess what to learn next
Lessons in Python, TypeScript, Rust and Julia - the four languages used in real AI engineering

before: Learning AI engineering means stitching together blog posts, video courses and documentation, guessing what to learn next.
Free resources are scattered and unstructured. Paid ones are expensive and often more theory than code.
after: One free curriculum, 523 lessons, 20 phases from zero to production. Each lesson is code you run, not slides you watch.
A clear path: finish Phase 5 and you can build a chatbot. Finish Phase 15 and you can put a working AI system online.
uses_note: The curriculum is 5 months old with 63K stars and 114K readers in the last 30 days. Published testimonials from named learners who completed specific portions and reported results are absent - coverage is mostly 'here's what it is' rather than 'here's what I learned by doing it.'

pulse.history_note: Created May 1. The 30-day gain of +21.2K is from findarepo's measured data.

steps: [Open the curriculum](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com) and start with Phase 0 if you're new, or jump to Phase 3 (Transformers) if you know the basics.
Pick any lesson, clone the repo, and run the file. Each one is self-contained: read the comments, modify the code, run it again.
Work through 3-5 lessons in a row to see how they build on each other.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch

If that scan passes: clone the repo, run 3 lessons from different phases (Phase 0, Phase 3, Phase 10). Report whether each lesson runs, whether the explanations are clear, and whether the exercises are useful. 15 minutes max.

footprint.disk: Clone the repo (size varies with full lesson history). Lessons are individual script files - small.
footprint.memory: Depends on the lesson. Early phases need only Python and a text editor. Later phases (GPU training, deployment) need more resources.
footprint.runs_on: Any computer with Python 3.x. Some lessons use TypeScript, Rust or Julia. GPU lessons (Phase 0, Lesson 3) need an NVIDIA card. Docker used in some deployment lessons.

best_for: You want to learn AI engineering hands-on, writing and running real code from day one, without paying for a course
You want a structured path from fundamentals to production, not a random collection of tutorials
skip_if: You learn better from video lectures and live instruction - this is text and code, no videos
You want a certificate or credential - this is a self-study curriculum with no formal assessment

alternatives.name: fast.ai
alternatives.line: Free video-based deep learning course. More established, with a strong community and forum, but less hands-on per lesson and focused on deep learning rather than the full AI engineering stack.

alternatives.name: Hugging Face Course
alternatives.line: Free NLP course built around the Hugging Face library. Narrower scope (NLP only), but deeper on that topic and integrated with the Hugging Face ecosystem.

watch: **Most coverage is by the creator.** Independent critical reviews are thin. The curriculum is comprehensive (523 lessons, ~342 hours), but hasn't been widely peer-reviewed.
**No completion testimonials yet.** 63K stars and 114K readers, but no named learner has published 'I did this curriculum and got a job / built a system / passed a benchmark.'
**One author.** Rohit Ghumare maintains the entire 523-lesson curriculum. Active development, but a large surface for one person.
**Later phases need real hardware.** GPU training, Docker deployments and multi-agent systems require more than a basic laptop.
